Figure 25 illustrates recent growth in U.S. SAF consumption. Domestic production and consumption were the same until 2020, when imported SAF entered the market. Domestic SAF production increased significantly in the past year from 39 million gallons in 2024 to 281 million gallons in 2025 (EPA 2025a). Despite these gains along with imports, domestic SAF consumption represents about 1% of domestic jet fuel consumption (EIA 2025d). There is considerable variability in the monthly availability of SAF, impacted by imports and economic conditions that may influence outputs from plants (Figure 26). Imports from Neste supplied 65% of U.S. SAF in 2024 but dropped to about 14% in 2025 (EPA 2025a). The decline in imports was anticipated due to changes in federal policy where foreign producers did not receive a production incentive, combined with a mandated SAF market that began in the European Union in 2025. Figure 27 shows that global production has doubled in each of the past 4 years.
